label: Doctor-bridge ordering contract is contradicted on the live advisor_recommend surface: command-doctor-env (score 0.540) ranks first above system-spec-kit (0.759606) and sk-doc (0.731278), both of which clear the same response's effectiveThresholds (conf 0.8 / unc 0.35) and are therefore passing skills. lib/scorer/fusion.ts:898 keepPassingSkillsAboveDoctorBridges should insert the passing bridge after min(2, passingSkillCount) passing skills, and the release note itself says a matching skill stays first even when three skills match. Mechanism unresolved: handler imports and calls scoreAdvisorPrompt (advisor-recommend.ts:17, :561) and the handoff is wired (fusion.ts:1368), so the divergence comes from the answering process or from passes_threshold being false in that run.

No locateable build artifact answers advisor_recommend: runtime/dist/lib/scorer/fusion.js does not exist while the source file is current, so the v4.0.0.12 promise that a stale advisor build fails with the build command instead of passing quietly cannot be checked, and an operator facing output that contradicts source has no artifact to diff and no path in the response naming where the answering code lives.

advisor_recommend omits passes_threshold, the single field keepPassingSkillsAboveDoctorBridges decides on (fusion.ts:898), so a reviewer who sees a low-scoring doctor bridge above two higher-scoring skills cannot tell a contract violation from a hidden threshold failure; exposing the field or an orderingRule note would have reduced f-iter011-001 to a one-line check.
